ask_view.py.gotcha: Nothing IMPORTS it — the join is a FILE (.view_request.json), read by control_app.view_request(). ask_view.py.purpose: Writes .view_request.json naming ONE console pane the console should bring to front once, so a human eye can photograph it; the harness has eyes and no hands.

auto_scope.py.gotcha: It REPORTS scope and decides nothing — it cannot arm, stop or change a lane. `forbids` is the load-bearing half of each LANE entry: only those words are enforced against the function's reachable source, so a prose-only claim like 'never deletes' is worthless unless the forbidden word is listed.
auto_scope.py.purpose: Declares what each automatic lane MAY touch, NEVER touches and how often it wakes — and checks every claim against the lane's own source.

bake_seed.py.gotcha: The board is NOT in Chrome — Chrome holds a months-stale copy. It reads pywebview/WKWebView sqlite (UTF-16-LE values) under ~/Library/WebKit/com.apple.python3/…/LocalStorage, and the three origin dirs must be copied to SEPARATE dirs or the small ones overwrite the board and it cheerfully reports zero. bake_seed.py.purpose: Bakes bible.html's shipped _GRAIL_SEED / _SET_SEED from his LIVE board store (WebKit sqlite) so a fresh profile shows real progress; reports unless --write.

blueprint.py.gotcha: `--check` REFUSES and never regenerates — the pre-push hook grades the WORKING TREE, so a hook that rewrote BLUEPRINT.md would dirty the tree it is grading. blueprint.py.purpose: Generates BLUEPRINT.md from the tree itself — capture doors, lanes, ledgers, readers, wilson lanes, rulings, the gate index, the river and the printer stream.

board_identity_sweep.py.gotcha: The standing ritual `rm -f tv/.board_identity.json after any CDP session` is WRONG for an `ok` record: removing his live owner record degrades ok->unknown and the next write starts a fresh id with `previous: None` — the exact shape that makes his real board render as a stranger's world. It also REFUSES while his console is running (port probe), and 'no file' reports UNKNOWN, not success. No production module imports it; only its gate test and the CLI.
board_identity_sweep.py.purpose: Classifies `.board_identity.json` as DRIFTED / GUEST / OK / UNKNOWN and sweeps only the first two, backed up first.

board_sync.py.purpose: Derives the task board from TASKS.md + git log — PENDING / IN PROGRESS / YOUR CALL / BLOCKED / COMPLETED with real commit author-dates — emitting adds and updates only; undecided rows are ORPHANED, never pruned.

build_runeword_roster.py.gotcha: `build()` STAMPS sourceHash, it does not CHECK it. Staleness is only detected by `is_stale()`, which nothing on the machine called until v2455 — the one roster lane of three with no watcher. build_runeword_roster.py.purpose: Regenerates tv/runeword_roster.json from bible.html's `const RUNEWORDS`, and reports whether that roster has gone stale against the page.

bump_version.py.gotcha: The note lands in a SINGLE-QUOTED JS literal inside bible.html, so an apostrophe (v1478 blanked the 37k-line page) or a callable CSS token `var(--x)` is refused rather than escaped. bump_version.py.purpose: Writes one vNNNN into all four stamps at once - bible.html D2R_BUILD.id, tv_diablo.VERSION, WINDOWS_SHIP.json ver, control_app /api/status ver - verifying each; refuses apostrophes and var(--x).

chronicle_calibrate.py.gotcha: The fill is a WATCHDOG calibrated to about ±1.5 points, never the exact percentage — it exists to catch a 3-point disagreement (0.8395 measured against a printed 85%), so quoting it as the figure is the misuse its own docstring forbids. It is structural pixel measurement, no OCR and no model call.
chronicle_calibrate.py.purpose: Reads the Chronicle completion BAR's gold fill from captured frames and sets it beside the board's own tally to catch calibration drift.

chronicle_crop.py.gotcha: It does NOT claim the crop reads better — v1780 measured crop 5/6 vs full 0/6, and v1829 measured one frame the crop refused twice that the FULL frame read fine. Both measurements stand and the transience is still open; the point is that both lanes get the SAME pixels and the framing is recorded. The band numbers live in chronicle_template — this file must never carry a second copy. Writes only to a temp file and degrades to the full frame on any failure.
chronicle_crop.py.purpose: The ONE Chronicle list-band crop that BOTH reading lanes use, and it stamps onto the page which framing each lane actually read.

chronicle_crossref.py.gotcha: canon() is the COMPARISON key only, never a display name: it folds curly to straight apostrophes because 202 of his names carry a straight one and 4 a curly one and bible.html holds BOTH byte forms of the same names — raw-byte compares file one item as two and inflate 'new'. chronicle_crossref.py.purpose: Answers whether reel-read item names are actually NEW or already in his ledger — 347 proposed names crossrefed to 319 already-owned, 28 new.

chronicle_doctor.py.gotcha: UNKNOWN is not a failure and must never be rendered as one. A check that raises is caught and returned as UNKNOWN ('the check itself failed'), never as MISSING — 'I could not check' and 'it is broken' are different sentences.
chronicle_doctor.py.purpose: Doctor for the chronicle arc — OK/MISSING/UNKNOWN per check on THIS machine: Grok login, footage, grouping, board apply. Never fixes.

chronicle_hunt.py.gotcha: It deliberately does NOT hunt neighbouring frames in the SAME reel — witnesses() returns a SET, so a 7th frame in a reel already tagged cross-frame changes nothing and the name stays held forever. Aiming at other reels is the whole point (cross-reel = independent pixels). `read_page` is INJECTED, so this module never decides how a page is read; `targets_for` defaults to ledger="uniques", so a sets hunt must pass kind ending in "sets" or it searches the wrong evidence (v1917 bug). Bounded at MAX_PER_NAME=18 frames per name, and it breaks after the FIRST hit.
chronicle_hunt.py.purpose: The focused re-hunt: for a HELD grail name, brackets where its Chronicle row must lie in OTHER reels and re-reads only those frames to earn a cross-reel witness.

chronicle_rebuild.py.gotcha: It rebuilds the LEDGER STORES, never the tally — re-deriving funiScan's 292 here produced 298 because `_norm` is a different fold from `_regKey`. Also: a store the caller could not read must be passed as None, NOT {} — {} means 'empty', None means 'unknown', and rebuild() refuses to collapse them. And it WRITES NOTHING; the board presses its own door.
chronicle_rebuild.py.purpose: Derives each owned name's date and provenance from the OTHER ledger stores (foundLog/gameFound/rwMade/evidence) under DATE_AUTHORITY, and returns a proposal — a rebuild, not a snapshot replay.

chronicle_regate.py.gotcha: `control_app.chronicle_regate()` is a DIFFERENT function with the same name that only re-scores in memory — this module is the ONE writer (test_provenance.py:501 pins that). Its whole reason to exist is the stamp: `_chronAutoAdopt` dedupes on `proposal.startedTs`/`savedTs`, so a re-gate done by hand keeps the ORIGINAL savedTs and the board silently refuses every newly grounded name with a message that reads like success. `regate()` is pure; nothing is written without `--write`.
chronicle_regate.py.purpose: Re-judges stored chronicle evidence under current rules and re-publishes it with a FRESH savedTs stamp so the board's adoption dedupe fires.

chronicle_resolve.py.purpose: Folds raw Chronicle reader names — OCR slips (Naglring→Nagelring), base-item debris, truncations — onto unique_roster.json before witnesses are counted; unresolvable names are RETIRED with a reason.

chronicle_retro.py.gotcha: LAW 1: this module cannot write AT ALL, and test_chronicle_retro proves it from the source text — which is why index recovery lives in reel_index.py and persistence in shadow_ledger.py. Also: STILL_MAX_DIFF=0.22 does NOT keep a scrolling read in one run (it shatters it); `known_chronicle` is the door that rescues those frames.
chronicle_retro.py.purpose: Retro Chronicle sweep engine — groups sealed-reel frames into still runs, reads only the Chronicle pages, returns a merge-max grail proposal.

chronicle_routes.py.gotcha: It carries NO table of routes — routes are discovered from disk, and its corroborator only BADGES a divergent sibling, it enforces nothing. routes() is memoised twice (in-process _MEMO plus .chronicle_routes_cache.json) because a cold derive cost 16.1s, so a stale cache is what you read unless cache_reset() runs.
chronicle_routes.py.purpose: Derives each chronicle route's lanes from the *_roster.json artifacts on disk and grades them FLOWING/WATCHED/DARK/UNKNOWN in the heart's vocabulary.

chronicle_sweep_now.py.gotcha: No module imports it — it is the command-line twin of the in-console sweep watchdog, and test_control gates its SOURCE TEXT for copy-drift against control_app's rule. Without --yes it only PRICES the work and exits; it proposes names and never applies them; and since v1832 a LIVE capture session is no longer a refusal (it skips only the one reel still growing).
chronicle_sweep_now.py.purpose: CLI that runs control_app's own chronicle sweep over unread reels without opening the console; capped at --max reels, no re-arming loop.

chronicle_template.py.gotcha: The v1690 docstring still says the three consumers are DELIBERATELY NOT WIRED and to 'expect zero hits' — that is stale: chronicle_retro, control_app, corroborate, health_engine, lane_lock and chronicle_crop all import it today. Also `detect_from_ocr_lines()` exists but is a WEAK SECONDARY that must never be the classify source (full-frame OCR returns the tooltip's text, not the panel chrome). Its tab vocabulary is intentionally its own — it says `sets`/`uniques` where route_totals says `set` and lane_lock says `uniques`; one_name.py exists to reconcile the three. Bands were measured only on the 2940x1912 calibration film; other aspects go through `_scale_band_for_aspect`, labelled derived-not-measured, and `signals['band_branch']` records which branch ran.
chronicle_template.py.purpose: Locked pixel geometry of the CENTERED Chronicle modal — colour-fraction bands per tab — resolved to uniques/sets/runewords with a stated why.

chronicle_total.py.gotcha: NOT the same file as route_totals.py, and nothing imports it — it is a hand-run record plus recipe (`--count uniqueitems.txt`), written because the OUTPUT was lost once when /tmp/casc_extract died. 403 is correct and the in-game panel reading of 404 in bible.html's own comment was a MISREAD. The game file itself is deliberately not committed (public repo, Blizzard data). 396 distinct names vs roster 398 is an OPEN measurement, not a defect.
chronicle_total.py.purpose: Banks the dated CASC re-derivation of the Chronicle denominator — 439 rows minus 24 disableChronicle = 415, minus 12 unspawnable = 403 — and re-derives it from uniqueitems.txt.

ci_sim.py.purpose: Runs the suite with the host things a GitHub runner lacks (his recorded board, his footage) stubbed and names which tests depend on his Mac; green means 'no KNOWN host trap', never 'CI will pass'.

code_identity.py.gotcha: It CANNOT be built from mtime and size - that is exactly what CPython uses to decide a .pyc is fresh, so a check from the same two inputs agrees with it by construction, collisions included. The only witness that survives one is co_firstlineno, which comes from the BYTECODE while the source is read fresh. Three instrument bugs on the way, each caught by a count: functools.wraps copies __module__ onto a wrapper whose code lives in contextlib (two unrelated modules both reported drifted at the SAME line 242), CPython points co_firstlineno at the FIRST DECORATOR so accepting any '@' line swallowed everything, and skipping COMMENT lines while walking to the def let a function that had moved 40 lines be re-found and reported clean. Decorators and blanks only. And on this Mac the cache is NOT in __pycache__ - sys.pycache_prefix puts it under ~/Library/Caches/com.apple.python.
code_identity.py.purpose: Answers whether THIS interpreter's loaded bytecode agrees with the source on disk, by comparing each function's co_firstlineno against where the file says it starts. Built after three pushes of one identical tree read green, RED, green, with the red one's traceback naming a line and a variable that do not exist in the file. Distinct from console_doctor's 'running code matches disk', which asks the CONSOLE over the wire about its own image.

code_staleness.py.gotcha: It CHANGES and BLOCKS nothing — no reload, no restart, no button. And a module that never called snapshot() answers UNKNOWN, not FRESH: 'nothing snapshotted' is not the same as current. snapshot() is a one-shot no-op on re-call by design — re-snapping would adopt today's disk as the baseline and the watchdog could never report STALE again. Its real purpose is `registry_may_be_incomplete`: it separates 'I do not know this evidence source' from 'this source may not exist', the conflation that made a 16-hour-old console accuse its own .self_arming.jsonl of forgery.
code_staleness.py.purpose: The stale-image watchdog: records each watched module's (mtime,size) at first use and answers FRESH / STALE / UNKNOWN about whether this process still runs the code on disk.

coldread.py.gotcha: The staged copy MUST live at the repo root (`.coldread.tmp.html`): `git show` into a scratch dir makes every relative `art/…` src 404 — measured 50 broken images vs 5 — and the eye then reports a regression that does not exist. A tab switch is a 0.28s fade, so it waits for full opacity and measures it; a black capture, an unsettled panel or an over-baseline broken-image count STOPS the run (exit 2), because a look recorded through a broken instrument is worse than no look.
coldread.py.purpose: Stages a shipped bible.html AT THE REPO ROOT and screenshots tabs/widths/regions for the cold second-eye pass, refusing to hand over a bad frame.

comment_count_gate.py.gotcha: It deliberately is NOT a fuzzy 'number near a word' check, and the restraint is most of the design: four different counts near 'set pieces' (108 / 110 / 127 / 135) are all correct at once, so a fuzzy gate would be wrong four times and get switched off. Only claims whose subject is unambiguous are checked, each against a value parsed from the same file.
comment_count_gate.py.purpose: Gate: parses bible.html for counts asserted in prose comments and fails when a claim disagrees with the value measured in the same file.

confidence.py.gotcha: shadow() DECIDES NOTHING by construction — it reports wouldPass/agrees and no caller may branch on it; the disagreements are the product. wilson_lower(1,1)=0.207 not 0, and only n=0 returns 0.0. confluence() is ADDITIVE and deliberately NOT capped at 1.0, and an unknown tag scores 0 rather than a default. chronicle_retro re-exports these names, so the math already living there is a re-export, not a second copy.
confidence.py.purpose: The ONE home for Wilson lower-bound + confluence scoring — how sure we are given how many looks, and how many KINDS of evidence agreed.

conftest.py.gotcha: It is a CANARY, not a lock — it reports damage after the bytes are gone. The isolation API is `redirect_module_path` (patch the module ATTRIBUTE and assert it took); `os.environ[...]` inside a test is a no-op for constants bound at import, which is how chron_evidence.json went 525,187 -> 748 bytes.
conftest.py.purpose: Session-wide pytest canaries — fails the run if a test changed the bytes of gitignored live data or left a child process running.

console_doctor.py.gotcha: report() does NOT run the checks — every row comes back UNMEASURED, because the organ interface is asked about COVERAGE, not findings; only run()/report(deep=True) executes, and it reaches into his live window via /api/board_ownership (JS evaluated in the window he is looking at) plus ~2 min of SLOW checks. It REPORTS: --fix touches only the provably reversible, and it calls the other doctors rather than re-implementing their checks.
console_doctor.py.purpose: The EAGLE EYE: one pass over the RUNNING console; each check answers OK / MISSING(action) / UNKNOWN(why), never a bare boolean.

console_healer.py.gotcha: Silent means OFF — without TV_AUTO_HEAL=1 it still scars everything and only reports what it WOULD have done. A heal that leaves the check red disarms that remedy for the life of the process; returning "nothing to do" is NOT a failure (v2080 retired a working remedy that way).
console_healer.py.purpose: Scar ledger plus three re-derivable remedies: fold orphan frames into the reel their own stamp names, restore a vault store from a healthy backup, clear a stale theatre-fault. TV_AUTO_HEAL arms it.

console_safe.py.gotcha: It is the single most-imported module here — 457 files call it — and it only works if called FIRST, before anything prints. Three separate regressions (REG-044, REG-054, REG-077) were correct code reporting FAILURE because the success branch died inside print('✅ …'). Any new tv/*.py entry point that prints non-ASCII needs the line; nothing enforces that automatically.
console_safe.py.purpose: enable() rewraps stdout/stderr with errors='replace' so a cp1255 console cannot turn a passing gate's own verdict print into exit 1.

control_app.py.gotcha: Not an app shell. 32,388 lines / ~470 defs: the Kai OCR name-resolution engine (_kai_*), chronicle + vault sweeps, retention/prune, heart/eagle/rescue/drift loops all live HERE, not in the sibling modules named after them — 107 modules in tv/ import it as `ca`. It has NO module-level VERSION: the only stamp is the single `"ver": "v3089"` literal inside status_payload() (line 27608), bump_version.py refuses the file if it finds two, and test_control locks it to tv_diablo.VERSION.
control_app.py.purpose: The console process itself: serves :17772 (control_ui.html + ~65 /api/* routes), owns ON/OFF/SIM/STOP agent lifecycle, and runs 25 background loops.

corroborate.py.gotcha: Each invariant carries `prove` and selftest() drives every one to RED against synthetic inputs — a corroborator nobody has seen disagree is exactly the green that lies; UNKNOWN is reported as UNKNOWN, never as agreement.
corroborate.py.purpose: THE CORROBORATOR - cross-engine invariants asserting the engines AGREE (the frame deleter never looser than the reel planner, one `owned` against another); it never writes and never averages.

counter_ledger.py.gotcha: `load()` returns None, never an empty list — a consumer that reads 'the game was never asked' as 'the game agrees' is the exact failure this file exists to end. Every row carries `readAt`/`ageDays`, and `d2r_setPieces` is an UNDATED array of strings, so for most pieces the order of reading vs finding is UNKNOWN (`undated: True`) — not evidence for the accusation and not evidence against it.
counter_ledger.py.purpose: The game's Remaining page as a NEGATIVE ledger — the only reader that can subtract: falsifies board rows, derives owned-by-subtraction.

crest_loudness.py.gotcha: Its own docstring is STALE about the refusal: it says 'NO CHROME IS UNKNOWN… Exit 2 says nobody looked', but since v2430 no-Chrome returns 77 (SKIP, which run_gates counts apart from PASS and FAIL and requires declared in skip_ok=); exit 2 now only means the harness/PIL would not load. Ranking is by saturated-pixel DENSITY, not count or chroma×area — both of those simply elected the page's largest containers. It claims board ownership (`d2r_ownerClaim`) before measuring because a CDP probe boots as a GUEST with seeds suppressed.
crest_loudness.py.purpose: Measures, by SATURATED-PIXEL SHARE, whether the install crest out-shouts everything else above the fold on bible.html at 1440x1000 — a visual-priority gate.

crossfamily_claude.py.gotcha: It does NOT invent the look — it reads a verdict Claude wrote and banks attacks=1 only for a surface whose answer says the claim held. A seat that is signed out, over quota or silent banks NOTHING, because an unreachable eye is an empty seat and never agreement. --wait retries until 20:00 local, the window after the 19:00 renewal.
crossfamily_claude.py.purpose: Banks a recorded Claude verdict as a cross-family attack against the locks that already cleared their attack bar.

css_who_wins.py.purpose: CLI lookup over bible.html's top-level <style> rules: for a selector (and optionally one property) it lists every declaring block and says which last declaration actually wins.

dead_field.py.gotcha: It REFUSES NOTHING — no build fails, no button blocks; it is evidence for a reader. And below MIN_ROWS=30 a column of nulls is UNKNOWN, not clean, because a zero over rows that could not disagree measures the sample. The `WATCHED` entries are 3- OR 4-tuples (the optional 4th is a declared-null map), so indexing blindly at [3] breaks the older rows. Born from `reel_retention._tombstone` writing None 410/410 times.
dead_field.py.purpose: Reports fields present on every row of a watched store and filled on none — a dead field — as evidence on each heart read.

declared_vs_content.py.gotcha: Its verdict today is UNTESTABLE, not CLEAN — measured on his tree: 40 reels, 1 declaring a chronicle focus, that one carrying 0 surveyed panels, 0 disagreements. Zero disagreements over an unexercised sample measures the SAMPLE, not the routing law. Two sites DO route on a declared stamp and are NOT defects: chronicle_retro._declared_kind (the declaration picks the reader, the sweep then judges content) and reel_retention._vault_lane_owes (an ABSENT stamp HOLDS the reel — errs toward keeping).
declared_vs_content.py.purpose: A15 — checks that a reel's route is derived from its CONTENT, never from the declared `focus` stamp in index.json.

disk_report_crossfamily.py.purpose: Runs the cold attacks a non-Anthropic family designed on credible_pruned_mb (-0.0, 0.9 MB against an empty corpus, 2 MB against 1 MiB) as prune.reports' second, independent evidence kind.

disk_report_wilson.py.gotcha: Despite the name it NEVER prunes, never calls prune_once, never touches TV_AUTO_PRUNE and never measures a disk — it only attacks the REPORTER. Its earlier 24/24 was 24 identity assertions against a passthrough writer (REG-600); the proof now is that a validator stub which accepts everything scores 0/24. 'Refused' means prunedMb=None WITH a prunedWhy sentence; a bare 0 is a measurement, not a refusal.
disk_report_wilson.py.purpose: Attack harness proving the disk row REFUSES bogus freed-MB figures (NaN, negative, bigger than the corpus), and banks a Wilson score.

dom_probe.py.gotcha: It exports JS SOURCE, not Python behaviour — prelude() returns a string you prepend to a page evaluation; the only Python def in the file is prelude(). The five scars it encodes: `body *` includes <script>, a clip test on an INLINE element is meaningless (clientWidth 0), occlusion has a direction, selecting by text finds the wrong box, and never infer colour from a class name.
dom_probe.py.purpose: JS probe source strings (__leafText/__clipped/__covers/__painted/__quoted) that stop a DOM measurement answering an adjacent question.

end_routes.py.gotcha: Every one of the 410 tombstones records why: 'read (N pages) and sealed by BOTH lanes' — and for 395 of them BOTH clauses are FALSE. 96.6% of all end-route traffic went through the STRUCTURAL door, which means 'there is nothing here to read' (394 had pages:0, 392 had no vault seal), so the permanent record of an irreversible delete says the opposite of what happened. The doors are a DISJUNCTION and must stay one: conjoining them would have refused 96% of every journey ever taken. The header names only two doors; `unextracted_door` is a third, added 2026-09-13. It decides nothing and deletes nothing — a second prune authority is precisely what it refuses to be. HELD never hides an unasked door: `unasked` is reported with each gap measured None.
end_routes.py.purpose: The end-route predicate reverse-engineered from the 410 tombstoned reels: three independent doors (structural, semantic, unextracted), read-only.

engine_joins.py.gotcha: It proves a FIELD ARRIVED, not that this engine put it there — with no per-field provenance a JOINED means 'the answer is on the row'. And 'unjoined' is two different problems: NO_DATA names engines whose fix is CAPTURE not wiring (slot_identity: 0 of 1,065 deep rows carry a slot; main_character: he does not film the character panel), while WHY_NOT records engines deliberately outside the printer (reel_segments and frame_authority are joined INDIRECTLY and a second import would be drift). HUB_FANOUT=15 excludes control_app's 65 imports from making everything look joined.
engine_joins.py.purpose: Census of which per-reel engines are actually consulted by printer.py and which answer nobody — joinedness DERIVED by walking printer.py's own AST imports, never a hand-kept flag.

exec_hygiene.py.purpose: Stops the warm workers an os.execv relaunch would orphan (module globals holding a live Popen in .p with .stop()), and at boot reaps the children inherited from the replaced image BY PID. Called by control_app._before_exec at every exec site and first thing in main().
exec_hygiene.py.gotcha: Never a blanket waitpid(-1): it would steal the exit status of the console's own Popen children, and CPython reads ECHILD as returncode 0 — a failed child would report success. children_of() returns None (UNKNOWN) when ps cannot be read, never [].

extract_gap.py.gotcha: It never writes, and especially never a seal — back-filling one would forge the certification frame_authority exists to protect. And 'the names exist' is NOT 'a holding exists': `holding_possible()` is the law that decides which read names the extraction contract can actually take, and on his store it removes the loudest row on the report (45 Chronicle checklist entries). Any RECOVERABLE figure read without it is inflated.
extract_gap.py.purpose: Per reel, why extraction is blocked and how much gap is RECOVERABLE — seals lacking names the journal already read. It writes nothing.

extract_ui_icons.py.gotcha: A .sprite is a FRAME ATLAS, not one image — `total width` is frameW × frameCount, so the naive reader that worked for 611 single-frame item icons walks off the end of the buffer on the first UI sprite. UI icons are ANIMATED (3 frames to 27) and several start fully transparent, so it takes the MOST OPAQUE frame, never frame 0. Without the CascLib toolchain it exits 77 (SKIP) — a machine with no D2R install is not a failing machine; the committed PNGs are the artifact. `--check` verifies disk and extracts nothing.
extract_ui_icons.py.purpose: Pulls the console's tab and MINI icons out of the local 28GB D2R CASC install as art/ui_*.png, replacing system emoji with true game sprites.

fake_claude.py.gotcha: Not an importable API — it is a BINARY spoken to over a pipe, and its FILENAME is a contract: tv_diablo.py:3265 disarms the paid-subscription circuit by string-matching `fake_claude` in the binary blob, so renaming this file silently arms real billing during tests. fixture_ledgers.py.purpose: redirect() points TV_UNKNOWN_AGE and TV_EAGLE_SLOW at pid-scoped temp files for a TEST process, so suites that drive console_doctor / unknown_age never write his live eagle ledgers.
fixture_ledgers.py.gotcha: For test processes ONLY — production code must never import it. It fills only an UNSET variable, so an explicit per-test redirect in setUp still wins. Seven suites call it at import (v3470); test_no_test_writes_his_eagle_ledgers pins that by AST, and run_gates._LIVE_STATE now names both ledgers so CI FAILS on a write.

fixture_tmp.py.gotcha: For test processes ONLY - production must never import it (the law checks by AST). fleet_mask.py.gotcha: An ABSENT mask is not an EMPTY one — decode() returns None for absent and a list for present, and a caller that renders them the same will tell him his cousin is missing all 135 pieces the first time the box opens. Every mask carries a 12-char roster sourceHash fingerprint; a decode against a different fingerprint returns UNKNOWN, never a guess. ledger_spec() deep-copies `stores` because dict() is shallow (v2760: a returned spec mutated the module constant process-wide), and an unknown ledger is REFUSED, never defaulted to sets.

fleet_routes.py.purpose: Judges each fleet-card lane (getter→probe→total→unit) for sets/uniques/runewords as FLOWING/WATCHED/DARK/UNKNOWN, quoting route_totals and chronicle_routes.corroborate rather than its own copy.

frame_authority.py.gotcha: It REPORTS rather than acts (:450 'this replaces a deleter that ran automatically'); sig_diff was replaced, not retuned — three frames naming three different grand charms are pairwise 0.00000 apart, so a hover tooltip moves it by literally zero.
frame_authority.py.purpose: The ONE deletion authority over his footage - the FRAME deleter asks IS THIS FRAME EVIDENCE, and an unreadable store, unparsable name or missing index all resolve to KEEP.

frame_ref.py.gotcha: None from timestamp_of means NOT ESTABLISHED, not 1970: a reel's 5-digit random suffix and a 1-2 digit index are rejected by the 12-14 digit epoch window, and a `15_1787496136628#v` suffix is still read by taking the leading digit run.
frame_ref.py.purpose: The one resolver for the three shapes a frame is addressed by: journal frameId 21_1787522052389, top-level f_<ms>.jpg, and reel-relative <reel>/f_<ms>.jpg. A failed match is None, never 'deleted'.

frame_release_wilson.py.gotcha: It banks under a NEW lock rather than under prune.arm on purpose — prune.arm is 'may the prune RUN' and vault.apply is the write door, so filing frame-granularity attacks there would move a bigger counter and prove nothing. It calls exactly one pure predicate on in-memory dicts: it never touches the seal store, apply_plan, _prune_once, os.remove/unlink/rmtree or TV_AUTO_PRUNE, and test_frame_release_wilson.py asserts that by reading this file's own source. Each entry is ONE distinct refusal idea, not a parameter sweep — five spellings of a falsy flag count as one.
frame_release_wilson.py.purpose: Wilson evidence for the `frame.release` lock — pure sabotages proving seal_releases_frames() refuses a bare 'nothing was taken' seal.

frozen_frame_watch.py.gotcha: GROUP BY GEOMETRY or the verdict is meaningless — the shelf holds 383 PNGs across eight geometries (full windows AND header/footer/rail crops), so 'hash the newest N files' compares a header crop against a footer crop and reports NOT FROZEN from a comparison that could never go red. It also does NOT take rows[1]: it takes the newest frame MIN_GAP_S or more older, because a copied file is identical by definition. It says FROZEN, never 'blank' — blank is a content claim only an eye can make. No frames = UNKNOWN, never healthy.
frozen_frame_watch.py.purpose: Detects a dead-but-200 console from the PIXELS — two consecutive byte-identical captures of the same window geometry means the screen stopped painting.

frozen_frames.py.gotcha: FROZEN and BLANK are never merged, and collapsing them is the defect. A repeated hash is a POINTER, not a verdict — it says the feed stopped moving and says nothing about what is on screen; a window can be frozen on a perfectly painted frame, and blank while its titlebar clock still ticks so every frame differs. The blankness bar is quoted from `paint_witness.verdict()`, never re-typed here.
frozen_frames.py.purpose: Reads capture files for two separate states: FROZEN (repeated sha256 of bytes) and BLANK (decoded pixels judged by paint_witness).

g5_grok_eyes.py.gotcha: API-style secrets are stripped from the child env on purpose (_API_STRIP) — this is the subscription CLI lane, never api.x.ai; OFF is an instant no-op returning None, and chronicle_doctor treats an unimportable g5 as 'the second eye is unavailable', never as agreement.
g5_grok_eyes.py.purpose: The second eye's vision lane: `grok -p` on his SuperGrok login, off/shadow/primary, reading the same area/tz/scene/names/names_loc/sockets JSON under an hourly+daily budget.

g5_shadow_reducer.py.gotcha: READ-SIDE ONLY. It never writes the shadow log and never prefers a lane: a 67.6% disagreement rate is a finding about the INSTRUMENTS, not a vote to settle. One-sided rows (only one lane answered) are NOT disagreements and are counted separately; rows where neither answered are not evidence at all. A rate with no denominator is UNKNOWN, never 0.0.
g5_shadow_reducer.py.purpose: Reduces tv/.g5_shadow.jsonl - the 6,082 Claude-vs-Grok rows written since 2026-08-23 that nothing had ever read - into an agreement report carrying its own denominator and window.

gate_costs.py.purpose: the MEASURED CI seconds of every gate (tv/gate_costs.json), so run_gates --shard balances the CI matrix on real cost instead of declared timeout.
gate_costs.py.gotcha: A measurement with a source, committed so every machine cuts the same slices. A gate the table has not seen weighs the MEDIAN, not its declared timeout. Refresh from CI job logs with python3 tv/gate_costs.py <logs>; test_the_gate_set_shards_cleanly refuses a table covering under 95% of the registry.

git_quiet.py.gotcha: Git for Windows' PATH git (Git\cmd\git.exe) is a 46 KB CUI WRAPPER and pythonw owns no console, so a CUI child ALLOCATES one — a real terminal on top of D2R. MEASURED 2026-09-21: windows stealing focus 2-3 in a row every couple of minutes. CREATE_NO_WINDOW on the wrapper is NOT enough because it respawns the real git without the flag, and headless-git.exe still starts a CUI git.exe child — so this calls mingw64\bin\git.exe DIRECTLY. It is a module rather than a helper inside control_app because console_doctor spawns git too and a second copy would drift; test_windows_git_spawns_hide_the_console pins that there may only ever be ONE body of the mingw redirect.
git_quiet.py.purpose: The ONE door every git spawn in this codebase walks through, so no git child ever owns a console.

guest_fixture_pack.py.gotcha: A pack is NOT a copied reel: one reel measured 196 MB / 153 frames, a pack of it is 2.7 MB / 16, spaced EVENLY so the scrub bar still travels the whole run (a head slice leaves the reel controls untestable past the opening). ⚠ A fixture gets its OWN namespaced sessionId — keeping the source's made the loader dedupe it against the real session list and the real row won, so the fixture flag never reached the guest. load() refuses any destination under tv/frames: a pack may be BUILT from footage and never LOADED into it.
guest_fixture_pack.py.purpose: Turns one recorded reel into a versioned, checksummed regression pack the guest seat can click: a representative subset of frames, flagged as a fixture, loadable only into a mirror.

guest_profile.py.gotcha: The rewrite is a REDACTION, not a relabel. The guest seat renders a mirror of the live console and this repo is public, so scrub() walks dict KEYS as well as values — per-session dumps are KEYED by path, and a values-only walk leaks the home directory one filename at a time. The identity is REPLACED rather than merged so an unknown key cannot ride along. ⚠ leaks() and the scrub read the SAME pair list, so a detector that forgets a secret is blind to it — callers must also check literals.
guest_profile.py.purpose: The Grok actor for the guest seat plus the redaction that keeps a public mirror publishable: a stable identity, and a deep scrub of the owner's install id, hostname, user and home paths out of every payload the box will serve.

handoff.py.gotcha: ⚠ THE WATERMARK MOVES ONLY WITH --mark, NEVER BY DRAINING - so reading the queue can never mark an unanswered ACT as read. Measured 2026-09-18: #180 held 1,177 comments / 2.55 MB and was taking 140 comments a day against 10 replies; the watermark drain is 65.5x cheaper. It still drains the CLOSED queues 179/180 on purpose, because the GrokBot native seat kept posting there after the rotation to #230.
handoff.py.purpose: Drains the GrokBot/Grok handoff queues in O(new) rather than O(all), using a stored watermark plus the REST `since` parameter, and sorts each comment into ACT / ASK / FYI so a brief cannot be lost in a wall of watch ticks.

health_engine.py.gotcha: IT REPORTS AND NEVER REPAIRS (a test pins that nothing here writes, deletes or restarts) — and it is not an AUTHORITY either: frame_authority owns deletion, chronicle_retro owns grounding, this only reports on them. UNKNOWN is a first-class state and never renders as ok; a check that raises becomes UNKNOWN, not a failure.
health_engine.py.purpose: The console's one red/green flag engine: nine checks (lanes, armed_migration, board_join, orphans, shelf witnesses, shadow_watch, readers_agree, self_arming, lane_liveness) each returning ok/warn/blocked/unknown.

heart.py.gotcha: The FLOWING branch is documented as UNREACHABLE with real data: `scored` is keyed on the ORGAN rows' ids (lanes, readers, selfArming, board_join) while `watcher` is a LANE name (tvd-eagle-watch and siblings) — two disjoint vocabularies, so `scored.get(watcher)` is always None. So a 'WATCHED, go sabotage it' prompt names work that cannot land. Also: it NEVER writes or caches (a gate asserts the module opens no file), counts are derived not typed, DARK != UNKNOWN, and WATCHED is work owed, not a fault.
heart.py.purpose: Derives every self-running vessel into ONE vocabulary — FLOWING / WATCHED / DARK / UNKNOWN — from lane_census, health rows and the lock ledger.

heart2.py.gotcha: v1 asks whether the SYSTEM is healthy; v2 asks whether the INSTRUMENTS can still go red — measured 2026-09-08, the heart was green while 12 of 238 gates were red and 8 were blind. Tampering happens ONLY in a safe_copy.py sandbox (never cp -R: tv/ is 5,865 MB of footage and a full copy once caused ENOSPC), and it PROPOSES into .heart2_proposals.md — it never edits a guard. A gate that fails its CLEAN run is UNPROVABLE, not BLIND; a sabotage whose `find` matches ≠ `matches` is the usual culprit, so the match count is printed. It is a RATCHET (the unproven backlog may only shrink), not a ban.
heart2.py.purpose: HEART 2.0 — the census of the gates themselves: re-tampers every guard that declares a RED_PROOF in a sandbox to prove it can still go red, and classifies each as proven / blind / unproven / unprovable.

heart2_candidates.py.gotcha: It refuses far more often than it proposes — anchor shorter than 8 chars, zero matches, more than one match, or an unresolvable target file all abort with a named reason. It returns TEXT only: it never writes to a guard and never writes to a target file.
heart2_candidates.py.purpose: Derives a ready-to-run red-proof (sabotage) candidate from a gate's own assertIn literals, so the proposal is actionable instead of a name.

heart_map.py.gotcha: `--check` REFUSES and never regenerates, exactly like blueprint.py, because the pre-push grades the WORKING TREE. ⚠ And an unreadable input is a REFUSAL, never a zero: `_read` returns None (v3231 — it used to return "", so an unreadable control_ui.html gave an empty id set and would have BANKED a HEART.md claiming the console paints 0 surfaces). A watcher that cannot be read is named rather than skipped, because dropping it makes every surface it covers look UNWATCHED — a coverage collapse indistinguishable from a real one. `_why_unmeasurable` is TOLD what the caller found and must never re-read the file: bump_version replaces the surfaces atomically and regenerates this map in the same run, so a second look can see a healthy file and strip the reason out of the refusal (v3235).
heart_map.py.purpose: Derives HEART.md from the tree: every `id` the console PAINTS (the honest unit — a class may be shared by forty nodes, an id names one thing), and which of them any watcher mentions. UNWATCHED is not a defect; what is refused is a surface going unwatched SILENTLY, so the count is a ratchet that may not fall without a reason in heart_floor.json.

hover_calibration.py.gotcha: It drives NOTHING — hover_mode moves the pointer and this is a passive witness of it, and record_step swallows its own errors so it can never strand his cursor. With no steps recorded calibrate() returns None and says why rather than emitting a plausible constant, which would place every item in the wrong cell with total confidence.
hover_calibration.py.purpose: Records mini auto's (planned frame target, screen point) pairs while it hovers and derives the tooltip->cell offset slot_identity refuses without.

hover_drive.py.gotcha: There is NO click by CONSTRUCTION, not by setting — no mouse-down/up event is ever built, so no flag or future caller can make it press (a left click on an occupied D2R cell picks the item up). It aborts the moment the pointer drifts more than 6px from where it left it, because his hand on the mouse wins, and it converts each target through screen_point() one at a time so a dragged window cannot leave a stale batch of coordinates.
hover_drive.py.purpose: The only file that moves his pointer: hovers slot_identity targets to reveal tooltips, building kCGEventMouseMoved and nothing else.

hover_mode.py.gotcha: It exists because both ends already existed and nothing joined them — `hover_drive.walk()` had ZERO callers, so the button he was looking for did not render. Four stop conditions, three of them his: if HIS HAND touches the mouse the sweep aborts and the pointer is deliberately NOT restored (fighting him for it is worse than leaving it). `status()` returning running:False with stopped:None means it has NEVER RUN — a different fact from 'ran and finished', and the UI must distinguish them. start() refuses a second concurrent sweep.
hover_mode.py.purpose: Joins the hover PLAN to the pointer ACTUATOR: sweeps each occupied stash cell so the game renders its tooltip. It moves only — it never clicks.

hover_wilson.py.gotcha: THE DENOMINATOR IS SABOTAGE ATTEMPTS, NOT RUNS — an always-agreeing check may be perfect or INERT (vault_autoreel_tick ran every 45s for months at 100% agreement having swept nothing), so a claim nobody tried to break scores UNPROVEN, and UNPROVEN must not read as failing. It runs on synthetic RECTANGLES, not his screen: no cursor moves, no window opens, safe in CI and safe while he plays. It is a REPORT not a gate — run_gates invokes it with -c and it has no failing mode, so it always exits 0. bank_into_proof_queue folds by (lock, kind, src) so re-running REPLACES rather than inflating n; attempts=None banks NOTHING.
hover_wilson.py.purpose: Scores the MINI/hover autopilot's four independently-failing claims — COORDINATE, ANCHOR, READ, SLOT — with a Wilson lower bound and banks them into the self-arming lock ledger.

human_eyes_gate.py.gotcha: Nothing imports it — run_gates.py:4345 registers it as Gate('human-eyes', ... '--gate'). It does NOT perform the A13 contradiction check (a LOOKED observation vs the live console) because a gate has no running console; it asserts only proven/owed/readable. For its whole early life it was registered as `--prove` ONLY, so it sabotaged fixtures and never opened his real ledger. Exit 77 = declared SKIP (no ledger on this venue), which is not a pass.
human_eyes_gate.py.purpose: Gate over the human-eyes LOOKED ledger: proves the loop ran end to end and no brief is OWED past its patience. 77 = declared skip.

human_eyes_ledger.py.gotcha: All three of its file-IO handlers return None, never [] — swallow_census cites this file as the purest instance of the honest shape, because None lets a caller tell 'could not ask' from 'no briefs'; flipping them to [] is the RANK-1 defect the ratchet exists to stop. It stores `saw` (raw observation) separately from `conclusion` on purpose: a brief that returns a conclusion with no observation reads like evidence and is not — a Grok pass quoted PROJECT_VAULT_MANAGER.md accurately and reported the wrong gate numbers. The ledger (.human_eyes.jsonl, overridable via TV_HUMAN_EYES_LEDGER) is a runtime record and is gitignored.
human_eyes_ledger.py.purpose: Records the Grok-Bot human-eyes loop: which briefs were SENT, which came back with a raw OBSERVATION plus verdict, and which are still owed.

inventory_law.py.gotcha: Deliberately NOT a roster — it word-boundary-matches the words D2R itself prints, because a reader hands over OCR of a tooltip, not a database id. LOCKED is tested BEFORE consumable and the order is load-bearing: a *Scroll* of Town Portal is a consumable while the TOME is furniture, and a reader that saw both on one line must not get the tome demoted. It changes no behaviour — it exists to give the retro readers the answer control_app already had.
inventory_law.py.purpose: The hardcoded three-class item law — LOCKED furniture (Horadric Cube, tomes, Wirt's Leg, keys), CONSUMABLE (potions, scrolls, gold), and LOOT, the only class worth a register.

item_identity.py.gotcha: Two vocabularies for one item, on one axis: a QUALIFIER (Latent/Renewed) is IDENTITY and never folds; an apostrophe byte, a base-type tail and an unambiguous parenthetical are RENDERING and do. ⚠ The parenthetical is decided by MEASUREMENT, not punctuation — 'Athena's Wrath' is a unique and nothing else so '(set piece)' folds, while 'Crescent Moon' is a unique AND a runeword so '(amulet)' is the only thing separating two real items.
item_identity.py.purpose: The two vocabularies for one item: what the VAULT calls a physical thing and what the CHRONICLE calls a grail line, separating identity from rendering so a Latent charm never witnesses a renewed one and an apostrophe byte never splits a row in two.

journal_drain.py.gotcha: It refuses far more often than it writes, and every refusal is deliberate. It will not run without an explicit yes, will not run if a backup did not verify row-for-row, will not run if the corpus moved since the plan judged it, and will not rename its rewrite over a file whose INODE changed — tv_diablo rotates the ring with os.replace, which makes sessions.1.jsonl GROW, so a line count cannot see it. Identity comes from os.fstat of the handle it read, never from the path.
journal_drain.py.purpose: The WRITER half of the journal drain: it backs up every generation of the session journal, removes the rows a plan released, and carries forward anything the recorder appended while it was writing. It exists as its own module because test_a_journal_row_leaves_only_on_proof forbids the PLANNER from holding any write-capable call, so the planner decides and this acts.

journal_retention.py.gotcha: Name suggests the reel river; it is the OTHER half. The reel side is finished (20 reels, ROUTED 20, TOMBSTONE 0 — correct, all three refusal groups are legitimate) while his shelf still shows 419 journal rows, ~195 of which name film that no longer exists. 'No film at all' is HELD, not extracted — absence of film is not proof of extraction. And it DELETES NOTHING; the apply half is his decision. Four rows are never releasable: newest 8, film still on disk, reels the test suite opens by name, and undatable rows.
journal_retention.py.purpose: Classifies shelf JOURNAL rows as RELEASABLE (footageState == retired) or HELD, keeps the newest 8, and explains every hold. Writes nothing.

js_syntax_gate.py.gotcha: A hand-rolled tokenizer was tried and REJECTED — it reported 14-16 false problems on files that parse perfectly, because these pages use template literals with nested backticks, embedded HTML and regex literals a heuristic cannot tell from division. So it asks a real engine. And when no browser is available it SKIPS LOUDLY: a gate that cannot run must say so, never pass silently.
js_syntax_gate.py.purpose: Loads bible.html and tv/control_ui.html in a real JS engine (Chromium via CDP, or node) and fails on any SyntaxError — one bad escape or mid-line comment blanks the whole 37k-line page.

lane_census.py.gotcha: NOT every thread is a lane — a one-shot worker is a TASK and registering it would promise persistence it does not have, so 'started but not registered' is not automatically 'unwatched'. It carries its own `--prove` because an earlier ad-hoc version misclassified five `while True` `_loop` functions as one-shot and that answer was quoted into a GitHub issue.
lane_census.py.purpose: Classifies every threading.Thread target in control_app.py as LOOP / one-shot / UNKNOWN, and diffs that census against BLUEPRINT.md's LANES section.

lane_health.py.gotcha: The stall thresholds are an explicitly LABELLED judgement, tuned against nothing. It decides nothing and writes nothing, and an unreadable store answers UNKNOWN rather than healthy — it exists because a watchdog that spoke only on message-change made five days of silence read as fine.
lane_health.py.purpose: Per extraction lane: freshness (when it last produced work), reach (corpus covered), and divergence (two lanes disagreeing about the same session).

lane_liveness.py.gotcha: _TICKS is PROCESS memory — a cold import outside control_app reports all 20 vessels UNKNOWN, which is a fact about the reader, not the lanes; use stamping_functions(), which parses the SOURCE and answers from anywhere. The period travels WITH the stamp (a global threshold spans 0.5s to 900s, 1800x), and every_s vs dead_after_s are two different questions — padding every_s makes the report print a period the lane does not have. Ages are monotonic so a sleeping Mac is not eight hours of silence.
lane_liveness.py.purpose: THREAD-ALIVE for console loops: each loop ticks with its OWN period; rows grade FLOWING/LATE/UNTIMED/UNKNOWN/DORMANT.

lane_lock.py.gotcha: lane_for() returns None rather than picking when a frame looks like BOTH a stash and a chronicle page — that is the deliberate behaviour, not a failure to decide, because the two wrong answers are not symmetrical (a Chronicle row filed as ownership claims he owns something he only saw listed). A cheap pixel gate is NOT sufficient: measured 2026-08-18, `classify_stash_grid` calls a real Chronicle page 'stash' with frac_dark 0.5364 and 11 dark columns, and only the AI classifier gets it right. The v1999 scar: `personal` and `shared` — the two tabs he is in most — were missing from the tab tuple, so ambiguous frames were not seen as ambiguous and the lock stayed OPEN.
lane_lock.py.purpose: One key from one frame: at most ONE write lane is ever unlocked — the vault surface OR exactly one chronicle ledger — and ambiguity locks both.

lane_trace.py.gotcha: A TICK IS NOT A SECOND WITNESS — lane_liveness._TICKS is an in-process dict on a monotonic clock and reads EMPTY from another process. A bare heartbeat would be an ECHO of the watchdog, so this must carry the RESULT: a loop running and producing nothing then reads as a CONTRADICTION, which is the only thing this organ can see. Writes are atomic (tmp + os.replace) because a plain open(p,'w') truncates first and an empty file reads as 'the loop produced nothing'. With min_gap_s the TRACE period is the GAP, not the tick period, and loop_corroborate.LOOPS must declare the gap or a correctly-throttled loop reads stale. note() swallows everything and returns False.
lane_trace.py.purpose: Writes one small per-lane file recording WHAT A LOOP DECIDED (drift verdict, orphan count, shadow result) so an outside process can date the loop — the second, independent witness a corroborator needs.

ledger_authority.py.gotcha: `onOwnerSeed` is ONE boolean answering a THREE-ledger question — it is UNSPECIFIC, not over-broad, and cannot say which of sets/uniques/runewords is actually inherited. The two scopes are never mixed: the local board is MEASURED name by name, fleet rows are DERIVED from counts and marked `derived: True`. And the seed totals are read from a live table, not a constant — a hardcoded _GRAIL_SEED goes stale the moment he plays.
ledger_authority.py.purpose: One manager over sets/uniques/runewords: per-ledger seed vs his own finds, staleness, manual accept/revoke, and the exit path off a seed.

ledger_highwater.py.gotcha: It exists because the doctor compares only the TWO NEWEST snapshots — take three snapshots after a loss and the pairwise diff goes clean while the items are still gone. A peak is not a diff. ⚠ The window BEGINS AFTER the incident that inspired it: snapshots start at foundLog 412, so the 391→383 loss is outside them — a clean window is not a clean history, and it prints that limit rather than filing it away. It shipped GREEN (0 consecutive drops), so it is insurance, not a live bug. `--seed` records today as the peak; `--accept KEY "why"` is the only way to lower one, and requires a reason.
ledger_highwater.py.purpose: Ratchets a STORED PEAK per ledger key (foundLog, owned, setPieces, rwMade) so the chronicle counter can only go up, and names anything now below its high-water mark.

ledger_restore.py.gotcha: Only foundLog and setPieces can travel back. `owned`, `rwMade` and `gameFound` are BACKED UP but NOT restorable here, and `/api/vault_apply` looks like the door for `owned` and is not — it re-gates any caller-supplied proposal through `_vault_retro()` (3 witnesses, 0.55 confidence floor), a gate added in v1595 that must not be widened for this. Backups written before v2731 carry no route and are SKIPPED with a reason rather than guessed at. Writes nothing; the restore is manual on purpose.
ledger_restore.py.purpose: Joins the automatic ledger backup to the board's own apply door: matches a backup by its STAMPED ROUTE, diffs it against the live board, and shapes the gap into `{wouldAdd:{uniques,sets}}`.

live_miss_audit.py.gotcha: It does not test the readers and never touches a camera — it only replays what the journal already recorded, and is built to run on ANOTHER machine's sessions.jsonl (that is where the cousin's failure lives). A stashTab of `""` and a VAULT tab both count as 'not identified as a tally tab', so B fires on both; only runes/gems/materials are tally tabs.
live_miss_audit.py.purpose: Reads the session journal and names WHICH of five links broke when a stash went unread: A no panel, B no tab named, C no intake fired, D empty, E worked.

live_panel_gate.py.gotcha: BELOW-FOLD is REPORTED and never failed — his 660px console window is deliberate design, so content below the fold is normal; only ZERO-HEIGHT and OFF-SIDE are RED. A console it cannot reach is UNKNOWN (exit 2), NOT a pass. It exists because render_check.py grades a seeded FIXTURE that lays out differently from the app — at 1120x628 the gate saw taskforce at y=224 h=30 while the live console had it at y=1050 h=502; both instruments were right about different pages. second_eye_run.py.gotcha: `sentCode` must be measured from the PROMPT TEXT by this script — hand-filling it put a typed 7,250 into an evidence ledger whose real value was 7,366, because code_was_transmitted() handed a dict returns the honest {chars:0}. second_eye_run.py.purpose: Runs a cold cross-family review of a shipped version end to end — finds the commit, strips the diff's comments, MEASURES the payload it is about to send, asks, and records the answer into second_eye_ledger.

self_arming.py.gotcha: k and n count SABOTAGES, never agreements — a lock fed by an agreement rate opens because nothing was ever tested, which is the exact failure it exists to prevent. `n == 0` is UNPROVEN, not failing. `may()` checks the ORDER first and reports the blocked upstream prerequisite rather than its own score, so a high number never reads as 'nearly there'. self_arming.py.purpose: The lock ledger: banks sabotages ATTEMPTED vs guard refusals per surface, scores them with Wilson + confluence, and answers may(lock) in his required order.

sets_base_index.py.gotcha: The uniques mechanism could NOT be copied: ITEM_CODEX carries a `base` for only 14 of the 135 set pieces. sets_base_index.py.purpose: Maps a BASE item name back to the SET PIECES still to find, the sets-side counterpart of bible.html's _chUniquesOnBase, so a reader can keyword-search for what is left.

shadow_ledger.py.gotcha: It exists only because chronicle_retro's LAW 1 forbids writing — chronicle_retro SCORES, this PERSISTS, the console REPORTS. It NEVER promotes the shadow rule on its own statistics, never reports a count without naming the diverging items, and never starts a fresh count over a file it could not parse. Its path goes through the fixture root (TV_HIST) — it did NOT before v2420, and 14 tests were writing his real ledger.

shelf_corroborate.py.gotcha: The dossier is the odd witness every time (52 of 53 reels on first run): control_app._theatre_sessions counts JOURNAL ROWS in the group, not film, and replay.split_sessions then divides those rows across duplicate groups — a label naming another quantity, split by a second bug. It REPORTS and never repairs, because making two witnesses agree by editing one buries the contradiction.
shelf_corroborate.py.purpose: Compares three independent witnesses to one reel's frame count — dossier, shelf card, f_*.jpg counted fresh on disk — and reports where they disagree.

shelf_driver.py.gotcha: It holds NO second predicate on purpose — it carries retention's own tag and why through untouched, because every serious 2026-09-10 defect was two authorities answering one question (41 vs 0, 40 vs 0, 2 vs 19). soak_test.py.gotcha: It is a top-level SCRIPT, not a unittest — nothing imports it; CI runs it via tv-soak.yml. Run bare on his Mac it pins a process for THIRTY minutes (TV_SOAK_MINUTES default 30) and binds port 17958; use TV_SOAK_MINUTES=2 locally. space_warden.py.gotcha: It is an OWNER, not a policy — the 9.5 GB Playwright blowout happened because test-results/ had no owner, while three pruners each owned something else. Above FLOOR_GB (default 20, TV_SPACE_FLOOR_GB) it does nothing at all unless forced, and `reclaim()` defaults to dry_run=True.
space_warden.py.purpose: Reclaims only REGENERABLE output when free space drops under FLOOR_GB, re-verifying each path is inside the repo, git-ignored and untracked; proposes the rest.
