store_owners.py.gotcha: It does NOT prove single-writer, and that is stated first because it is what a reader assumes. Two attempts to measure writes — a filename-adjacency grep and an AST walk resolving constants — BOTH returned zero writers for all four stores, which measured the instruments rather than the code (paths are bound in helpers and threaded through arguments). What it checks is a ratchet: every store names an owner whose source actually mentions it, every other toucher is a declared reader WITH A REASON, and a new toucher fails. Consumers read the `STORES` dict directly; there is no `report()` function despite one being referenced by name in write_census.py's comments.
store_owners.py.purpose: Declares ONE owner plus reasoned readers for each reel store and fails any undeclared module that touches one — coupling evidence, not a write proof.

surface_precision.py.gotcha: precision() returns None for 'not established' and that is NEVER 0.0 — below MIN_SAMPLES a zero means nobody looked. Unmeasured combinations still get READ ('that is how they become measured'); only a combination MEASURED over a real sample to yield nothing is refused. Two counter-intuitive measured facts live here: the ocr lane produced ONE real name in 1,136 placed sightings (it earns its keep on STRUCTURE, not names), and a CHRONICLE PAGE is the BEST naming surface there is (45 real of 74) — a gate built on 'chronicle = bad' would have discarded his best source, because precision and PROVENANCE are orthogonal and a chronicle page lists items he does not own. The table's own history is a trap: REG-439's 'correction' re-queried a ROTATED sessions.jsonl holding a fifth of the ring (REG-440); recount() exists so the table cannot rot.
surface_precision.py.purpose: What a read name is WORTH given its lane and surface — a measured Wilson lower bound per (lane, surface) that sets how many witnesses it needs and whether a paid read is worth spending there.

surfaces.py.gotcha: Techniques are (name, params) tuples and never call-shaped text: tv/test_reachability.py counts that shape to find functions with no caller, so a declaration written as a call made an orphan read as alive — and the warning about it tripped the same scanner when it quoted the bad example.
surfaces.py.purpose: 7 in-game surfaces in one table: stash/runes/gems/materials/inventory (stash_eye, left-anchor), chronicle-uniques/-sets (chronicle_template, centre modal), each with its enlarge and tooltip need.

swallow_census.py.gotcha: A RANK IS A PLACE IN A QUEUE, NOT A VERDICT — it cannot tell you a site is wrong, and reporting a rank as a defect would make it the very thing it was written to stop. Most of the 537 are CORRECT (`try: tab.close() except: pass` should swallow). Two refusal paths matter: a MISSING baseline prints 🔴 and returns 1 ('unconfigured is not clean'), and since v2389 a baseline whose counts.rank1 is not an int is MALFORMED, not a count of zero — that bug once reported a healthy tree as '74 NEW sites'.
swallow_census.py.purpose: AST census of swallowed exceptions ranked by whether the handler hands a caller a FALSY DEFAULT after a failed read — and a ratchet gate that fails only when the RANK-1 count grows.

sweep_wilson.py.gotcha: It shares the 'A2 · step 1' label with printer_wilson but guards a DIFFERENT lock — vault.sweep_start (bar 0.510, the door that spends his money) versus printer.stream. It swaps _CHRON_JOB and _chron_lanes only inside a finally, and `limit=None` is deliberately untested because None legitimately means ALL.
sweep_wilson.py.purpose: Proves the PAID sweep door refuses: chronicle_sweep_start must reject busy, no-lane, a limit of -5/0/'x', and a non-existent hist dir. No attempt has a success path. Banks under vault.sweep_start.

tasks_freshness.py.gotcha: It never edits TASKS.md — editing fixes today and drifts again next ship, which is why the table sat 34 versions stale. The fingerprint (`<!--fp: bible.html :: fv.onclick-->`) is the string whose PRESENCE means the work is undone, so the gate inverts the usual sense. Fingerprints are anchored and COUNTED, not grepped, because a correction note describing a fixed bug satisfies a naive search for that bug. Only the undone/READY tables are graded; shipped tables are history. `--prove` makes it go red for its own reason.
tasks_freshness.py.purpose: Gate: a TASKS.md READY row whose fingerprint string has vanished is finished work still listed as ready; unfingerprinted rows are named UNKNOWN.

tooltip_crop.py.gotcha: It answers WHERE the picture changed, never WHAT it says — a crop is evidence to LOOK at, not a second witness; counting it as one would double-count the single look that produced it. A diff covering more than MAX_FRAC (0.45) of the frame is a tab change or a reel cut and is REFUSED rather than cropped; below MIN_FRAC (0.002) it is JPEG noise. Unlike #31 (slot identity) this needs no calibration and no schema change — vault_retro already recorded that on a tooltip pass only the tooltip rectangle changes. Requires PIL.
tooltip_crop.py.purpose: Finds the tooltip rectangle on a hover run by differencing consecutive frames, and crops it, so the receipt that NAMED an item can be shown beside the item.

tooltip_find.py.gotcha: It finds the tooltip by TEXT DENSITY, not darkness and not a border — the D2R tooltip is semi-transparent with soft edges and 48.7% of his frame is near-black. Below `min_lines` it returns None deliberately (an unhovered frame and an empty one are the same honest answer). `bank(named=None)` is PENDING and counts in neither side. tooltip_find.json is live state, not a test artifact.
tooltip_find.py.purpose: Locates the D2R tooltip in one frame by OCR text density over a tile grid, returning a crop rect or a refusal, and banks a Wilson score on whether a located tooltip was really one.

trace_spine.py.gotcha: Follows ONE named item across reel -> ledger -> routing -> endpoint, and asserts the NEGATIVE half too: a chronicle or farming scenario must produce ZERO vault rows. ⚠ It REPORTS and never writes — footage has no un-delete and the witnessed machinery stays the only writer.
trace_spine.py.purpose: Follows one named item across reel, ledger, routing decision and endpoint, and proves the negative half: that a chronicle or farming scenario deposits nothing in the vault.

tree_busy.py.gotcha: ⚠⚠ TWO SIGNALS, AND THE LOCK ALONE IS NOT ENOUGH. run_gates takes the flock, but the hook runs renders, console demos and the Playwright smoke OUTSIDE that claim - MEASURED during the v3328 push, the flock read FREE while a pre-push had been grading 15 minutes with smoke in flight. ⚠ UNKNOWN IS NOT FREE, and EITHER signal going dark is enough: the first cut used `and` so a blind flock plus a clean process list fell through to free with the primary signal silent - the second eye found it, and the law could not have, because it stubbed both signals as None. ⚠ The process probe matches an INVOCATION, never a MENTION: `pgrep -f hooks/pre-push` also matches `vi hooks/pre-push`, which would refuse every bump while an editor stayed open. ⚠ It RELEASES the flock the moment it has tested it - holding it would make the checker the second gate run REG-162 is about. ⚠ Its reach is bounded and stated: an ad-hoc heredoc that writes bible.html directly will never consult a module it does not import.
tree_busy.py.purpose: Answers ONE question with ONE definition: is this working tree being graded right now? `hooks/pre-push` grades the WORKING TREE rather than the commit, so a version banked mid-run gets a green verdict about bytes that are not the ones shipping. bump_version consults it and REFUSES to stamp when the answer is anything but free. It returns a REASON string rather than a bare bool, so the refusal can say which signal fired.

tv_diablo.py.gotcha: PROMPT_VER (p1839) must bump whenever READ_PROMPT changes or older seals never get reopened; _parse_read DROPS out-of-vocabulary values into _parse_audit rather than keeping them (names_loc only equipped|inventory|stash|floor, sockets only int 1..6) — 'what the model SAID vs what survived'.
tv_diablo.py.purpose: ON AIR autopilot (capture -> vision read -> bridge) and the READ_PROMPT contract it parses and audits: area, tz (the TERROR ZONE, read off the purple terror-zone lines), scene, stashTab, chronicleTab, names, names_loc, sockets, discovered, conf.

unify_census.py.gotcha: MINI AUTO (the hover technique) is deliberately out of scope — his #17/#41, reserved to him. And `reproduced=None` means nobody looked: it is not False and emphatically not True, and may_unify() refuses on it exactly as it refuses on a measured gap.
unify_census.py.purpose: Prerequisite for deleting MINI (the time-boxed ONE-focus capture): AST call-graph over control_app proves every MINI technique, template and scenario exists under ON AIR; UNKNOWN blocks may_unify().

unknown_age.py.gotcha: It STAMPS only — it never promotes UNKNOWN to ok or missing because time passed; an UNKNOWN that ages is still UNKNOWN. _load() distinguishes None (file exists and will not parse = UNKNOWN, and attach() must not _save over it) from {} (no file yet = measured-empty). path() reads TV_UNKNOWN_AGE at CALL time, so tests can redirect it.
unknown_age.py.purpose: Stamps firstUnknownTs/lastAttemptTs/unknownCount onto UNKNOWN health rows so a 5-minute and a 45-hour unknown stop rendering alike.

vault_apply_crossfamily.py.purpose: Runs the cold attacks a non-Anthropic family designed against vault.apply's write door (an uncorroborated row under `unsure` bypassing the re-gate; owned=None) and banks them as the cross-family kind.

vault_backup.py.gotcha: A backup that was never read back is not a restore. Its copies are only as good as the verification that follows them — see the RESTORE work in task #81, which measured that nothing reads these saves back.
vault_backup.py.purpose: Copies the vault's stores aside before anything mutates them, so a bad apply has somewhere to come back from.

vault_bank.py.gotcha: The ONE reader for the stash-side bank. It folds two different 'empty' wordings and REPORTS that it folded them, so a caller cannot mistake a fold for a measurement.
vault_bank.py.purpose: The one reader for the stash-side bank, reporting what it accumulated and saying out loud when it folded two different wordings of empty into one.

vault_corpus.py.gotcha: The loose frames/hist ROOT (883 frames) and the 27 REELS the sweeps walk (1,970 frames) share ZERO filenames — they are separate archives, and every stash measurement before this file was taken on the LOOSE half that no sweep has ever walked. REG-185's '0 of 17 reels declare an ownership surface' never meant 'there is no stash footage', only 'no reel DECLARED one'. The INVENTORY works because 10x4 is KNOWN and ENFORCED — the refusal does the work and the pitch fit only has to agree — so there is deliberately NO stash lattice: RotW's stash dimensions are unrecorded and any stash occupancy would be a guess dressed as a measurement. Gold text alone does not find the title; the tight fraction WINDOW does (lobby, in-game menu and Chronicle panel all print gold). _fit() can return None and callers must not unpack it blind (v2799).
vault_corpus.py.purpose: Indexes which frames of his reels show an ownership surface and which stash tab is active, then fits the 10x4 inventory lattice and reads per-cell occupancy — pixels only, no vision spend.

vault_doctor.py.gotcha: Free by construction — local pixel work only, no model turn, no console, no network — so it can run while the console is down, which is exactly when someone asks. Doctrine borrowed wholesale from chronicle_doctor: OK / MISSING / UNKNOWN, and UNKNOWN is 'I could not check', never 'it is broken'. It samples (SAMPLE_EVERY=12, SAMPLE_CAP=240 frames), so 'no stash panels found' is a sampled answer, not an exhaustive one.
vault_doctor.py.purpose: Why the vault is empty, from his own film and free: no footage vs no stash panels vs panels with no readable names. Reports, never fixes.

vault_fixture_reels.py.gotcha: Every frame must have DISTINCT pixels, not just distinct names: vault_simulate.run passes sig=chronicle_retro.jpeg_sig and the sweep dedupes on that signature, so two byte-similar frames collapse into one and a scenario silently loses a witness — hence `signatures_are_distinct` as a first-class check. It exists because the armed prune deleted 123MB of reels NAMED in vault_simulate.py: the retention rule for 'the test suite opens this by name' globbed only tv/test_*.py, and vault_simulate.py is the module that DEFINES what the tests run. The rule restored is the mirror image of the usual one — live data management must not be able to eat the fixtures.
vault_fixture_reels.py.purpose: Materialises tiny synthetic reels (real JPEGs + index.json, ~30KB per tree) for the vault scenarios, so the suite never again holds gigabytes of his real footage hostage.

vault_fixture_unsorted.py.gotcha: Nothing in the tree imports or runs it — it is a hand-run design fixture. It PROVES itself before being trusted: stresses_the_real_edges() fails the fixture unless it has 50+ names, an 8-character length spread and BOTH apostrophe bytes, because a fixture that renders tidily certifies a layout the real data will break. It falls back to a named hand-written spread when the catalogue cannot be read — never to a silent empty list — and as_localstorage() returns a string it never writes, so aiming a harness at his real profile is the caller's bug to avoid.
vault_fixture_unsorted.py.purpose: Builds a SYNTHETIC 215-pill unsorted dock from the real bible.html catalogue so the Vault Manager's layout can be designed without touching d2r_owned.

vault_retro.py.gotcha: Independence is counted in SESSIONS, not still-runs — two still-runs inside one reel are ONE witness looking twice at the same stash, so a single-session reel can never ground a name however confident the reader is. It NEVER writes: `apply_payload()` only shapes a proposal for the one existing apply (window.chronicleApply), which owns the stamp, merge-max and undo. throwOut clears a strictly higher bar on BOTH axes because there is no un-throw in Diablo. All thresholds (STILL_MAX_DIFF, MIN_RUN_FRAMES, the still-run grouping) are imported from chronicle_retro, not restated.
vault_retro.py.purpose: Retro sweep of sealed reels into an owned / unsure / throwOut vault proposal: merge-max across sessions, two-SESSION witnesses, honest-absent, never writes.

vault_simulate.py.gotcha: Only the READER's answer is injected — the frame names, timestamps, still-run grouping (via chronicle_retro), the real gate and the real merge are all the production code, because the archive contains everything except what a reader would have said. The rule it exists to make visible: seeing an item MORE often never means throw it away — repetition decides OWNERSHIP, and only the reader's own junk flag can propose a discard, and then only across three separate recordings. So the scenarios deliberately include cases that SHOULD refuse. It calls console_safe.enable() at import because a non-ASCII print on his Windows console crashes the script while reporting a clean tree.
vault_simulate.py.purpose: Drives the vault lane end to end on his REAL reels with a scripted reader injected, printing the whole ownership/discard decision in the Vault manager's own words — no vision calls, no writes.

vault_wilson.py.gotcha: It never applies anything: every row carries an EMPTY evidence list, so the v1595 re-gate refuses before the board is ever asked. Banking is OPT-IN (`--bank`) because an audit that writes evidence is not an audit — and there are TWO bank doors, the shared `bank_into_proof_queue` and a separate LIVE-witness bank in main(); guarding only the first still moved his ledger. `vault.forget` is UNPROVABLE by construction (no refusal path) and `forget_note()` says so rather than leaving a blank.
vault_wilson.py.purpose: Sabotage harness for the `vault.apply` lock — six proposals the write door must refuse, Wilson-scored offline and again against the running console.

vault_witness.py.gotcha: Nothing in the console, heart or doctor calls it — only its own gate imports it and store_owners names it in a prose registry string, so the reading it produces reaches no surface. The hole it watches is real: control_app.vault_apply's re-gate lives inside `if caller_supplied` and the console button posts `{}`, so a result gated under an older bar applies as-is (6 of 7 rows, measured). AGE is context, never a verdict — the verdict comes only from the re-gate disagreeing.
vault_witness.py.purpose: Holds the vault's STORED owned rows beside a re-gate of their own witnesses at today's live bars, and publishes the disagreement.

verdict_provenance.py.gotcha: The census figures are RESTATED in eight places and five of them went stale (41/4/3/21/12/1 in prose against the tool's own 44/6/4/16/17/1), so every restatement must carry the DATE it was measured. REFERENCE (a clockless roster or lookup table) is NOT a missing stamp — the first cut had no REFERENCE class and cried '18 of 21 missing' with 24 unreadable subjects, measuring itself. ratchet() is red only if the gap GREW, and it returns 1 (UNKNOWN, not clean) when the baseline is absent, unparseable, or predates trackedNames.
verdict_provenance.py.purpose: Census over the console's stores asking whether each stored verdict names WHAT produced it: ANSWERS/PARTIAL/SILENT/REFERENCE/UNKNOWN.

version_stamp_gate.py.gotcha: STAMPS must learn any fifth surface bump_version learns — its first draft listed only three and would have passed a tree whose control_app stamp was left behind. It reads only the LEADING version cluster, so `revert what v1900 broke` is not judged, and a subject naming no version passes in silence.
version_stamp_gate.py.purpose: Reads the last commit SUBJECT: if it names vNNNN, the four stamps (D2R_BUILD.id, tv_diablo.VERSION, WINDOWS_SHIP.json, control_app ver) must equal the HIGHEST named. Writes nothing; silent when none.

win_relaunch.py.purpose: Makes a console relaunch and boot leave a trace on every OS (tv/.console_boot.log, tv/.relaunch_receipt.json) and, on Windows where os.execv starts a new pid, makes the child wait for its parent to exit before it takes the primary mutex and binds :17772.
win_relaunch.py.gotcha: Never raises into the boot path. wait_for_parent pops TVD_RELAUNCH_PARENT so it cannot leak into the next relaunch; on POSIX the parent is the same pid and nothing is waited for. Windows behaviour was measured on the ALT box, not simulated.

window_visibility.py.gotcha: THREE ANSWERS, NEVER TWO: None = could not establish (no Quartz, an exception, no window of ours), and None must never read as False — 'nobody looked' and 'it is not there' are opposite facts. It exists because document.visibilityState is CIRCULAR: WebKit throttles a hidden window's timers and the heartbeat IS a timer, so from the first hidden beat the rescue is disarmed forever. Window LISTING needs no Screen Recording grant — only capturing pixels does — which is why it is not screenshot-based on this Mac. REG-594: a window listed on screen and covered 100% by Citrix Viewer used to return True and reloaded a healthy console seven times in one day; a covered window CONFIRMS a hidden beat. And UNKNOWN occlusion is not permission — it returns False.
window_visibility.py.purpose: Asks the OS (CGWindowList) whether his console window is really on screen and whether another app is covering ≥95% of it — an independent witness the page's own heartbeat cannot supply.

windows_boot_check.py.purpose: Boots a SCRATCH console (TV_STUB=1, TV_CAPTURE=off, own port and sandbox) and asks /api/status which build it runs, against tv/WINDOWS_SHIP.json. The Windows CI job (tv-windows-boot.yml) runs it on windows-latest (#229).
windows_boot_check.py.gotcha: Exit 77 = could not run (no manifest), never a pass. TVD_BOOT_CHECK_TREE points it at another tree, which is how it was proven on the ALT over SSH without touching his checkout. The console is stopped by its own PID and the sandbox removed whatever happens.

write_census.py.gotcha: Nothing imports it — run_gates.py:3399 registers it as Gate('write_census'). A store nobody exercised reports NOT EXERCISED WITH A REASON, never '0 writers' (the tombstone needs a real deletion and the prune stays OFF; vault stores need a PAID sweep). Every exercise runs against a scratch root, never his stores. The only witnessed event comes from the `os.replace` patch, because these stores are written as <name>.tmp then moved — three earlier instruments each returned a zero that measured themselves, and it once shipped a false green by calling a `store_owners.report()` that does not exist.
write_census.py.purpose: Arms write_witness over a REAL write to a scratch root and reads back WHO wrote each reel store — observation, not coupling declaration.

write_witness.py.gotcha: It ONLY observes — it records and calls straight through to the originals, never redirecting, blocking or fabricating a write. ⚠ And it PROVES NOTHING UNTIL SOMETHING RUNS under `with watching()`: enabling it does not gather evidence, so the per-store answer is a measurement nobody has taken yet — which is not the same fact as 'one writer'. It exists because two static detectors (filename-adjacency grep, AST constant-resolution) both returned ZERO writers for all four stores, measuring the instruments rather than the code. Related trap recorded in write_census.py: patching only `open` also yields 0 — this codebase writes via io.open.
write_witness.py.purpose: Runtime witness that patches open/io.open/os.replace to RECORD which module actually writes each watched reel store (vault_swept, vault_accum, reel_tombstones, retro_triage, chron_evidence).

his_answers.py.gotcha: A changed fingerprint REOPENS the question and keeps the old answer as stale history; ruled holds 30 days, snooze 7, handoff until the question changes. An unreadable store is reported and NEVER written over. The path is chosen by the console (_decision_path), so each machine keeps its own answers.
his_answers.py.purpose: Keeps his answers to the questions THIS console asked him (console_doctor.ASKS), one per question with the question's fingerprint, and applies them at read time so an answered question stops billing him and the row says what he chose.

item_tables.py.gotcha: THE STATS BLOCK AND AN ITEM USE DIFFERENT WIDTHS for the same stat: csvBits (character 'gf' section) vs saveBits (item bitstream) - strength is 10 bits in one and 8 in the other, and reading one with the other derails. A table KEY is not a display name: 97 unique keys differ from what the game prints (Thudergod's Vigor is Thundergod's Vigor), so names come from item-names.json / item-runes.json and `namesFrom` says which. runes.txt has no Runeword80, so the row and the RunewordN key disagree from row 80 on; both are stored and neither is picked. Never wrap the pull in the perl alarm idiom (see affix_lexicon).
item_tables.py.purpose: Generates tv/item_tables.json from the D2R CASC: exactly what tv/d2s_read.py needs to decode a character save - per stat id its item and character-save bit widths, per item code its display name, kind (armor/weapon/misc) and stackable flag, uniques and set items by *ID, and runewords by 1-based runes.txt row. load() returns None, never an empty dict, when it has not been generated.

d2s_read.py.gotcha: A PARTIAL ITEM LIST IS NEVER COMPLETE: the bitstream has no per-item length, so ok is True only when the declared TOP-LEVEL count (socketed children ride inside their parent) ends exactly on the corpse 'JM', the stats block ends on 'if', and the file's size and checksum hold. Format 105 adds ONE bit after the type-specific block and ONE bit after the last property list before byte-align - the study decoder's '8 bits after a runeword list' and sniffed '0x00 pad' are that same trailing bit on a list that ends on a byte boundary. A runeword past runes.txt row 79 is named None with both candidates, because row and key disagree there and no save has told which the game means.
d2s_read.py.purpose: Reads a D2R character save (.d2s, format 105) byte-exact: header (name, class, level, last played), the stats block by name, the 30 skill bytes, every item with location/slot/panel/x/y, code, name, quality, unique/set/runeword names, sockets and socketed children, ethereal, ilvl, defense, durability and properties as [{stat, param, value}], plus merc/golem presence and a verify block (bytesConsumed, endsOnCorpseTag, itemCount, stoppedAt).
